prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Katy, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1322; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision at the intersection in Katy. Is it all right if I record this conversation?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Could you describe where you were driving and which direction you were headed when the collision occurred?

A: I was heading east on the main road and approaching the signal at the cross street. The light was green for me, I'm pretty sure of that.

Q: What happened as you entered the intersection?

A: A vehicle came from my right, from the side street, and it didn't stop. It hit the passenger side of my car pretty hard. I didn't have time to react.

Q: Did you see that vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I glanced over maybe a second before it hit, but there wasn't much I could do.

Q: After the collision, did you feel any injuries right away?

A: My neck and shoulders hurt, but I thought I'd just been jolted. By that evening the pain was worse, and I had a headache that wouldn't go away.

Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next day. They said it looked like whiplash and gave me a neck brace and some medication. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: Are you still experiencing those symptoms?

A: Yes, some of the stiffness and headaches are still there, especially when I turn my head to check traffic or drive for a long time.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident?

A: Only that I was following the traffic rules and I'm hoping this can be sorted out quickly, since I'm still having trouble with work and daily tasks.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

A: Thank you.
